1. # AgriSense - Web Dashboard
2. 
3. ## 🚀 Project Overview
4. 
5. This project is the frontend web dashboard for the AgriSense intelligent irrigation management platform. It allows users to monitor sensor data, control irrigation systems, view predictions, and manage alerts in real-time.
6. 
7. ## 🏗️ System Architecture
8. 
9. ### Technology Stack
10. - **Core**: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)
11. - **Framework/Libraries**:
12.   - **Vue.js 3**: For building reactive UI components.
13.   - **Chart.js**: For data visualization (charts and graphs).
14.   - **Axios**: For making HTTP requests to the FastAPI backend.
15.   - **(Optional) Tailwind CSS**: For rapid UI development and responsive design.
16.   - **(Optional) Socket.IO Client**: For real-time communication if WebSockets are used extensively beyond Firebase Realtime Database listeners.
17. - **Build Tools**:
18.   - **Vite**: For an efficient development server, hot module replacement, and optimized production builds.
19. 
20. ### File Structure
21. ```
22. Frontend/
23. ├── public/
24. │   ├── index.html              # Main HTML file (entry point)
25. │   ├── register.html           # Registration page
26. │   ├── favicon.ico
27. │   └── ... (other static assets like images, icons)
28. │
29. ├── src/
30. │   ├── main.js                 # Application entry point, initializes Vue app
31. │   ├── App.vue                 # Root Vue component
32. │   ├── router.js               # Vue Router configuration
33. │   ├── components/
34. │   │   ├── SensorDisplay.vue     # Displays individual sensor readings
35. │   │   ├── IrrigationControl.vue # Controls for starting/stopping irrigation
36. │   │   ├── PredictionChart.vue   # Chart for future water needs
37. │   │   ├── LogsTable.vue         # Table for irrigation history
38. │   │   ├── AlertsBanner.vue      # Displays critical/warning alerts
39. │   │   ├── UserProfile.vue       # User profile display/edit
40. │   │   ├── AdminPanel.vue        # Admin-specific UI components
41. │   │   └── ... (other UI components)
42. │   ├── services/

44. │   │   ├── auth.js             # Authentication logic (login, logout, token handling)

46. │   │   └── websocket.js        # WebSocket connection handling (if used)

63. 
64. ---
65. 
66. ## 📜 Features by User Role
67. 
68. ### 1. Farmer (Full Control)
69. - **Real-time Display**: Temperature, humidity, soil moisture.
70. - **Irrigation Control**: Status (ON/OFF), Manual Override (Start/Stop buttons), Mode selection (Auto/Manual).
71. - **Irrigation Logs**: History table with timestamps, duration, water used.
72. - **Future Predictions**: Charts showing water needs for the next 24-48 hours.
73. - **Alerts**: Critical warning banners for low moisture, sensor failures, etc.
74. 
75. ### 2. Middleman (View-Only Assistant)
76. - **View-Only Access**: All sensor data, irrigation status, logs, and predictions.
77. - **No Control Capabilities**: Cannot start/stop irrigation or change settings.
78. - **Multi-Device View**: Ability to view data from multiple assigned devices/farmers.
79. 
80. ### 3. Admin (System Control)
81. - **All Farmer Capabilities**.
82. - **User Management**: View, add, edit, and remove users; assign roles and device access.
83. - **ML Model Management**: Interface to retrain the ML model, view model version, accuracy, and download datasets.
84. - **System Health Dashboard**: Overview of all devices, sensors, and user activity.
85. 
86. ---
87. 
88. ## 🚀 Core Components & Functionality
89. 
90. ### 1. Authentication (`src/services/auth.js`, `public/index.html`, `public/register.html`)
91. - **Login Page**: Handles user login requests using the backend API.
92. - **Registration Page**: Allows new users to sign up with role selection.
93. - **Token Management**: Stores JWT tokens (e.g., in localStorage) and handles verification/refresh.
94. - **Protected Routes**: Ensures only authenticated users can access the dashboard.
95. 
96. ### 2. Real-time Data Handling (`src/services/firebase.js`, `src/components/`)
97. - **Firebase Integration**: Connects to Firebase Realtime Database or Firestore.
98. - **Listeners**: Sets up listeners to receive real-time updates for sensor data, irrigation status, and alerts.
99. - **Sensor Display Component**: Updates UI elements dynamically as new data arrives.
100. 
101. ### 3. Irrigation Control (`src/components/IrrigationControl.vue`, `src/services/api.js`)
102. - **Manual Controls**: Buttons for starting/stopping irrigation, with confirmation modals.
103. - **Mode Selection**: Toggles between Auto and Manual modes.
104. - **API Integration**: Sends commands to the backend API endpoints (`/irrigation/manual-start`, `/irrigation/manual-stop`).
105. 
106. ### 4. Data Visualization (`src/components/PredictionChart.vue`, `src/js/charts.js`)
107. - **Chart.js Integration**: Renders historical sensor data and future predictions.
108. - **Dynamic Updates**: Charts update in real-time as new data becomes available.
109. 
110. ### 5. Alerts (`src/components/AlertsBanner.vue`)
111. - **Display Logic**: Shows banners (Red, Yellow, Blue) based on alert severity.
112. - **Real-time Monitoring**: Listens for new alerts from Firebase or API.
113. 
114. ### 6. Admin Features (`src/components/AdminPanel.vue`, `src/services/api.js`)
115. - **User Management UI**: Forms and tables for managing users.
116. - **ML Model Interface**: Buttons/forms for retraining, downloading data.
117. 
118. ---
119. 
120. ## 🛠️ Setup and Installation
121. 
122. 1.  **Prerequisites**:
123.     - Node.js (v18 or higher recommended)
124.     - npm or yarn (v7 or higher recommended for parallel script execution)
125.     - Firebase Project Setup (Firestore, Realtime Database, Authentication enabled)
126. 
127. 2.  **Clone the Repository**:
128.     ```bash
129.     git clone <repository-url>
130.     cd Frontend
131.     ```
132. 
133. 3.  **Install Dependencies**:
134.     ```bash
135.     npm install
136.     # or
137.     yarn install
138.     ```
139. 
140. 4.  **Configuration**:
141.     - Create a `.env` file in the root of the `Frontend` directory.
142.     - Add your Firebase project configuration details and the backend API base URL.
143.     ```dotenv
144.     # Example .env file
145.     VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY
146.     VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=YOUR_AUTH_DOMAIN
147.     VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=YOUR_PROJECT_ID
148.     VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=YOUR_STORAGE_BUCKET
149.     VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=YOUR_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID
150.     VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID=YOUR_APP_ID
151.     VITE_FIREBASE_MEASUREMENT_ID=YOUR_MEASUREMENT_ID
152. 
153.     VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/v1
154.     ```
155.     *Note: Ensure all Firebase and API related variables are prefixed with `VITE_` for Vite compatibility.*
156. 
157. 5.  **Run Development Server**:
158.     ```bash
159.     npm run dev
160.     # or
161.     yarn dev
162.     ```
163.     This command starts the development server, typically accessible at `http://localhost:5173` (Vite's default). It includes hot module replacement for a smooth development experience.
164. 
165. 6.  **Build for Production**:
166.     ```bash
167.     npm run build
168.     # or
169.     yarn build
170.     ```
171.     This command generates an optimized production build in the `dist/` directory. The contents of this directory are ready for deployment.
172. 
173. ---
174. 
175. ## ☁️ Deployment Recommendations
176. 
177. - **Static Hosting**: Deploy the contents of the `dist/` folder to services like:
178.   - **Firebase Hosting**: Highly recommended due to seamless integration with Firebase services (Authentication, Firestore, Realtime Database).
179.   - **Netlify / Vercel**: Offer excellent CI/CD pipelines, global CDN, and easy configuration.
180.   - **AWS S3 + CloudFront**: A scalable and robust solution for hosting static assets.
181. 
182. - **CI/CD**: Implement a Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment pipeline (e.g., using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) to automate the build and deployment process upon code commits.
183. 
184. ---
185. 
186. ## 📄 Documentation
187. 
188. - **API Documentation**: Automatically generated by FastAPI and accessible via the backend's `/docs` endpoint (Swagger UI).
189. - **Code Comments**: Comprehensive inline comments are provided within the codebase to explain logic, component props, and service functions.

1. from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status, Request
2. from typing import List
3. from app.services.user_service import get_user_from_firestore
4. from app.middleware.auth import JWTBearer
5. 
6. security = JWTBearer()
7. 
8. def require_roles(required_roles: List[str]):
9.     """
10.     Dependency that checks if the current user has one of the required roles.
11.     """
12.     async def role_checker(request: Request, token: str = Depends(security)):
13.         user_payload = request.state.user
14.         uid = user_payload.get("uid")
15. 
16.         if not uid:
17.             raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Could not validate credentials.")
18. 
19.         user = get_user_from_firestore(uid)
20.         if not user:
21.             raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="User not found.")
22. 
23.         if user.role not in required_roles:
24.             raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="You do not have the required permissions.")
25.             
26.         return user
27. 
28.     return role_checker
29.

16. 
17.

21. 
22. public_keys_cache = {}
23. last_fetch_time = None
24. CACHE_DURATION_SECONDS = 3600  # Cache for 1 hour
25. 
26. def verify_token(token: str) -> Optional[dict]:
27.     global public_keys_cache, last_fetch_time
28. 
29.     # 1. Check cache for public keys
30.     if not public_keys_cache or \
31.        (last_fetch_time and (datetime.now() - last_fetch_time).total_seconds() > CACHE_DURATION_SECONDS):
32.         try:
33.             public_key_url = "https://www.googleapis.com/robot/v1/metadata/x509/securetoken@system.gserviceaccount.com"
34.             response = requests.get(public_key_url, timeout=5)  # Add a timeout for safety
35.             response.raise_for_status()  # Raise HTTPError for bad responses (4xx or 5xx)
36.             public_keys_cache = response.json()
37.             last_fetch_time = datetime.now()
38.             print("INFO: Fetched new Firebase public keys and updated cache.")
39.         except requests.exceptions.RequestException as req_e:
40.             print(f"ERROR: Failed to fetch Firebase public keys: {req_e}")
41.             # If we can't fetch new keys, try with existing cache if it exists, otherwise fail
42.             if not public_keys_cache:
43.                 return None
44.         except Exception as e:
45.             print(f"ERROR: Unexpected error while fetching Firebase public keys: {e}")
46.             if not public_keys_cache:
47.                 return None
48.     
49.     # Rest of the verification logic remains largely the same, using public_keys_cache
50.     try:
51.         unverified_header = jwt.get_unverified_header(token)
52.         alg = unverified_header["alg"]
53.         kid = unverified_header["kid"]
54. 
55.         key = public_keys_cache.get(kid)  # Use from cache
56.         if not key:
57.             print("ERROR: Public key not found in cache for kid.")
58.             return None
59. 
60.         # Verify the token
61.         payload = jwt.decode(
62.             token,
63.             key,
64.             algorithms=[alg],
65.             audience=settings.FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID,
66.             issuer=f"https://securetoken.google.com/{settings.FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID}"
67.         )
68.         return payload
69.     except JWTError as e:
70.         print(f"ERROR: JWT verification failed: {e.__class__.__name__}: {e}")
71.         return None
72.     except Exception as e:
73.         print(f"ERROR: Unexpected error during JWT verification: {e}")
74.         return None

200.     Update a user's preferences.
201.     Only the user themselves or an admin can update preferences.
202.     """
203.     user_payload = request.state.user
204.     acting_user_uid = user_payload.get('user_id') or user_payload.get('uid')
205.     
206.     # To get the role, we need to fetch the user's profile from Firestore
207.     acting_user = await get_user_from_firestore(acting_user_uid)
208.     if not acting_user:

210.

212.         raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Not authorized to update these preferences.")
213. 
214.     prefs_ref = firebase_service.db.collection('user_preferences').document(user_id)
215.     
216.     # For logging, get old preferences
217.     old_prefs_doc = await asyncio.to_thread(prefs_ref.get)
218.     old_prefs = UserPreferences(**old_prefs_doc.to_dict()) if old_prefs_doc.exists else UserPreferences()
219. 
220.     # Set the new preferences
221.     await asyncio.to_thread(prefs_ref.set, preferences.model_dump())
222. 
223.     # Log the activity
224.     changes = {k: {"old": getattr(old_prefs, k), "new": getattr(preferences, k)} for k in preferences.model_dump().keys() if getattr(old_prefs, k) != getattr(preferences, k)}
225.     if changes:
226.         log_activity(
227.             user_id=acting_user_uid,
228.             action="User Preferences Update",

26.   authStore.token = token;
27.   localStorage.setItem('accessToken', token);
28. }
29.

31.   authStore.user = null;
32.   authStore.token = null;
33.   localStorage.removeItem('accessToken');

6. 
7. class JWTBearer(HTTPBearer):
8.     def __init__(self, auto_error: bool = True):
9.         super(JWTBearer, self).__init__(auto_error=auto_error)
10. 
11.     async def __call__(self, request: Request):
12.         credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = await super(JWTBearer, self).__call__(request)
13.         
14.         if credentials:
15.             if not credentials.scheme == "Bearer":
16.                 raise HTTPException(
17.                     status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
18.                     detail="Invalid authentication scheme."
19.                 )
20.             
21.             token = credentials.credentials
22.             user_payload = self.verify_jwt(token) # Renamed to user_payload for clarity
23.             
24.             print(f"DEBUG: JWTBearer - verified user payload: {user_payload}")
25.             
26.             if not user_payload:
27.                 raise HTTPException(
28.                     status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
29.                     detail="Invalid token or expired token."
30.                 )
31.             
32.             # Attach user info to request for use in route handlers
33.             request.state.user = user_payload
34.             return token
35.         else:
36.             raise HTTPException(
37.                 status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
38.                 detail="Invalid authorization code."
39.             )
40. 
41.     def verify_jwt(self, jwtoken: str) -> Optional[dict]:
42.         try:
43.             # Use app.services.auth_service.verify_token for backend's JWT
44.             payload = verify_token(jwtoken)
45.             if payload:
46.                 return payload
47.                 
48.         except Exception as e:
49.             print(f"Backend JWT verification error: {e}")
50.         
51.         return None
```

32. async def handle_auto_irrigation(device_id: str, soil_moisture: Optional[float]):
33.     """
34.     Real-time irrigation control based on soil moisture threshold (AUTO) or user command (MANUAL).
35.     Only updates if state actually changes + debounce prevents rapid toggling.
36.     """
37.     try:
38.         control = await irrigation_service.get_control_state(device_id)
39. 
40.         # In MANUAL mode, we don't override the pump_state automatically.
41.         if control.mode == "MANUAL":
42.             return
43. 
44.         # --- AUTO MODE LOGIC ---
45.         if soil_moisture is None:
46.             return  # Skip if no soil moisture data in AUTO mode
47. 
48.         # Fetch system-wide thresholds for soil moisture
49.         settings_ref = firebase_service.db.collection('system_settings').document('alert_thresholds')
50.         doc = await asyncio.to_thread(settings_ref.get)
51.         
52.         # Use system threshold if available, else fallback to control-specific or 30.0
53.         threshold = 30.0
54.         if doc.exists:
55.             threshold = doc.to_dict().get("soil_moisture_critical", 30.0)
56.             print(f"DEBUG: Found system-wide threshold: {threshold}")
57.         elif control.threshold:
58.             threshold = control.threshold
59.             print(f"DEBUG: No system-wide threshold found, using device-specific: {threshold}")
60.         else:
61.             print(f"DEBUG: No threshold found, using default: {threshold}")
62. 
63.         # Decision: pump ON if moisture below threshold
64.         new_pump_state = soil_moisture < threshold
65.         print(f"DEBUG: Device {device_id} - Soil: {soil_moisture}%, Threshold: {threshold}%, Current Pump: {control.pump_state}, New Pump: {new_pump_state}")
66. 
67.         # ✅ Debounce: prevent rapid toggling
68.         now = time.time()
69.         last_change = _last_state_change_time.get(device_id, 0)
70.         if (now - last_change) < DEBOUNCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS:
71.             return  # Too soon, skip this change
72. 
73.         # Update control state
74.         control.pump_state = new_pump_state
75.         await irrigation_service.update_control_state(control)
76. 
77.         # Track change time for debounce
78.         _last_state_change_time[device_id] = now
79. 
80.         # Log only on actual state changes
81.         state_str = "ON" if new_pump_state else "OFF"
82.         print(f"💧 [Auto Irrigation] Device {device_id}: Pump turned {state_str} (moisture={soil_moisture:.1f}%, threshold={threshold:.1f}%)")
83. 
84.     except Exception as e:

1. import asyncio
2. import time

5. import pytz
6. from app.models.user import User
7. from app.services.firebase_service import firebase_service
8. 
9. # User cache to reduce Firestore reads
10. _user_cache = {}
11. _user_cache_time = {}
12. USER_CACHE_EXPIRY = 3600  # 1 hour in seconds
13. 
14. async def get_user_from_firestore(uid: str, include_deleted: bool = False) -> Optional[User]:
15.     now = time.time()
16.     
17.     # Return from cache if fresh
18.     if uid in _user_cache and (now - _user_cache_time.get(uid, 0)) < USER_CACHE_EXPIRY:
19.         # print(f"DEBUG: get_user_from_firestore - returning CACHED user with UID: {uid}")
20.         return _user_cache[uid]
21. 
22.     print(f"DEBUG: get_user_from_firestore - trying to fetch user with UID: {uid}")
23.     user_ref = firebase_service.db.collection('users').document(uid)
24.     
25.     # Use to_thread for blocking get()
26.     doc = await asyncio.to_thread(user_ref.get)
27.     
28.     if doc.exists:
29.         print(f"DEBUG: get_user_from_firestore - document found for UID: {uid}")
30.         user_data = doc.to_dict()
31.         if not include_deleted and user_data.get('is_deleted', False):
32.             return None
33.         
34.         try:
35.             user_data['id'] = doc.id # Add the document ID to the data
36.             user = User(**user_data)
37.             
38.             # Update cache
39.             _user_cache[uid] = user
40.             _user_cache_time[uid] = now
41.             
42.             return user
43.         except Exception as e:
44.             print(f"ERROR: get_user_from_firestore - Pydantic validation error for UID {uid}: {e}")
45.             return None
46. 
47.     else:
48.         print(f"DEBUG: get_user_from_firestore - document NOT found for UID: {uid}")
49.         return None
50. 
51. async def create_user_in_firestore(user: User):
52.     user_ref = firebase_service.db.collection('users').document(user.id)
53.     # Use to_thread for blocking set()
54.     await asyncio.to_thread(user_ref.set, user.model_dump(by_alias=True))
55. 
56. async def update_user_in_firestore(uid: str, update_data: dict):
57.     user_ref = firebase_service.db.collection('users').document(uid)
58.     # Use to_thread for blocking update()
59.     await asyncio.to_thread(user_ref.update, update_data)

61. async def get_all_users_from_firestore(skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100, include_deleted: bool = False) -> List[User]:
62.     users_ref = firebase_service.db.collection('users')
63.     query = users_ref.order_by('created_at')
64. 
65.     if not include_deleted:
66.         query = query.where('is_deleted', '==', False)
67. 
68.     # Use to_thread for blocking stream()
69.     docs = await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: [doc for doc in query.stream()])
70. 
71.     all_users = []
72.     for doc in docs:
73.         user_data = doc.to_dict()
74.         user_data['id'] = doc.id # Add the document ID
75.         all_users.append(User(**user_data))
76. 
77.     return all_users[skip : skip + limit]
78.

1. import asyncio
2. import requests
3. import os
4. from datetime import datetime
5. from dotenv import load_dotenv
6. from typing import Dict, Any, List
7. 
8. # Load environment variables from .env file
9. load_dotenv()
10. 
11. BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
12. 
13. ADMIN_EMAIL = os.getenv("ADMIN_EMAIL", "admin@example.com")
14. ADMIN_PASSWORD = os.getenv("ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin")
15. FIREBASE_API_KEY = os.getenv("FIREBASE_API_KEY")
16. 
17. async def get_admin_token() -> str:
18.     """
19.     Authenticates as an admin user with Firebase, gets an ID token,
20.     then uses that ID token to get a backend JWT token.
21.     """
22.     if not FIREBASE_API_KEY:
23.         raise Exception("FIREBASE_API_KEY not set. Please add it to your .env file in the backend directory.")
24. 
25.     # 1. Sign in with Email/Password to Firebase to get an ID Token
26.     firebase_signin_url = f"https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signInWithPassword?key={FIREBASE_API_KEY}"
27.     firebase_login_payload = {
28.         "email": ADMIN_EMAIL,
29.         "password": ADMIN_PASSWORD,
30.         "returnSecureToken": True
31.     }
32.     print("Attempting to get Firebase ID token...")
33.     try:
34.         response = requests.post(firebase_signin_url, json=firebase_login_payload)
35.         response.raise_for_status()
36.         firebase_id_token = response.json().get("idToken")
37.         if not firebase_id_token:
38.             raise Exception("Failed to retrieve Firebase ID token.")
39.         print("Successfully obtained Firebase ID token.")
40.     except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
41.         print(f"Error signing in with email/password to get ID token from Firebase: {e}")
42.         if e.response:
43.             print(f"Firebase response: {e.response.text}")
44.         raise
45. 
46.     # 2. Use Firebase ID Token to get the backend's JWT token
47.     login_url = f"{BASE_URL}/auth/login"
48.     backend_login_payload = {
49.         "id_token": firebase_id_token
50.     }
51.     print("Attempting to get backend JWT token...")
52.     try:
53.         response = requests.post(login_url, json=backend_login_payload)
54.         response.raise_for_status() # Raise an exception for HTTP errors
55.         token = response.json().get("access_token")
56.         if not token:
57.             raise Exception("Failed to retrieve backend access token.")
58.         print(f"Successfully obtained backend JWT token.")
59.         return token
60.     except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
61.         print(f"Error getting backend JWT token from /auth/login: {e}")
62.         if e.response:
63.             print(f"Backend response: {e.response.text}")
64.         raise
65. 
66. async def get_all_devices(token: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
67.     """
68.     Fetches all registered devices from the backend.
69.     """
70.     headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
71.     devices_url = f"{BASE_URL}/sensors/"
72.     print("Fetching devices...")
73.     response = requests.get(devices_url, headers=headers)
74.     response.raise_for_status()
75.     devices = response.json()
76.     print(f"Found {len(devices)} devices.")
77.     return devices
78. 
79. async def get_latest_reading_for_device(device_id: str, token: str):
80.     """
81.     Fetches the latest sensor reading for a specific device.
82.     """
83.     headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
84.     url = f"{BASE_URL}/sensors/{device_id}/latest-reading"
85.     print(f"Fetching latest reading for device {device_id}...")
86.     try:
87.         response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
88.         response.raise_for_status()
89.         print(f"Latest Reading for {device_id}: {response.json()}")
90.     except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
91.         print(f"Error fetching latest reading for device {device_id}: {e}")
92.         if e.response:
93.             print(f"Response content: {e.response.text}")
94. 
95. async def get_hourly_average_for_device(device_id: str, token: str):
96.     """
97.     Fetches the hourly average sensor readings for a specific device.
98.     """
99.     headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
100.     url = f"{BASE_URL}/sensors/{device_id}/hourly-average"
101.     print(f"Fetching hourly averages for device {device_id}...")
102.     try:
103.         response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
104.         response.raise_for_status()
105.         print(f"Hourly Averages for {device_id}: {response.json()}")
106.     except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
107.         print(f"Error fetching hourly averages for device {device_id}: {e}")
108.         if e.response:
109.             print(f"Response content: {e.response.text}")
110. 
111. async def get_daily_summary_for_device(device_id: str, token: str):
112.     """
113.     Fetches the daily summary sensor readings for a specific device.
114.     """
115.     headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
116.     # You can specify a date here, e.g., for today
117.     today = datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%d") # Use UTC now to match backend
118.     url = f"{BASE_URL}/sensors/{device_id}/daily-summary?date={today}"
119.     print(f"Fetching daily summary for device {device_id} (Date: {today})...")
120.     try:
121.         response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
122.         response.raise_for_status()
123.         print(f"Daily Summary for {device_id}: {response.json()}")
124.     except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
125.         print(f"Error fetching daily summary for device {device_id}: {e}")
126.         if e.response:
127.             print(f"Response content: {e.response.text}")
128. 
129. async def main():
130.     token = await get_admin_token()
131.     devices = await get_all_devices(token)
132. 
133.     if not devices:
134.         print("No devices found. Please ensure test devices are created.")
135.         return
136. 
137.     # Use the first device found for testing
138.     test_device_id = devices[0]['id']
139.     print(f"\n--- Testing endpoints for device ID: {test_device_id} ---")
140. 
141.     await get_latest_reading_for_device(test_device_id, token)
142.     await get_hourly_average_for_device(test_device_id, token)
143.     await get_daily_summary_for_device(test_device_id, token)
144.     
145.     print("\n--- Testing complete ---")
146. 
147. if __name__ == "__main__":
148.     try:
149.         loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
150.     except RuntimeError:
151.         loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
152.         asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
153.     
154.     print("Starting sensor endpoint tester...")
155.     try:
156.         loop.run_until_complete(main())
157.     except KeyboardInterrupt:
158.         print("\nSensor endpoint tester stopped.")
159.     finally:
160.         loop.close()
161.

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """
3. Test script to simulate ESP32 soil moisture data being sent to backend.
4. This mimics exactly what the ESP32 sends every 2 seconds.
5. 
6. Use this to verify:
7. 1. Backend receives data correctly
8. 2. Data is stored in Firebase
9. 3. ML is NOT triggered (commented out)
10. """
11. 
12. import requests
13. import time
14. import random
15. 
16. # Backend API URL
17. API_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
18. 
19. # Test device ID (same format as ESP32 generates)
20. DEVICE_ID = "esp32-DEMO-001"
21. 
22. def send_soil_moisture_reading(soil_moisture_value):
23.     """
24.     Send a single soil moisture reading to the backend.
25.     Mimics exactly what the ESP32 code sends.
26.     """
27.     # Correct endpoint: /sensors/{device_id}/readings (NOT /api/sensors/...)
28.     url = f"{API_BASE_URL}/sensors/{DEVICE_ID}/readings"
29.     
30.     # Payload matches ESP32 JSON structure (soil moisture only, others are 0)
31.     payload = {
32.         "device_id": DEVICE_ID,
33.         "soil_moisture": soil_moisture_value,
34.         "temperature": 0,      # Not testing DHT22 today - commented out in ESP32
35.         "humidity": 0,         # Not testing DHT22 today - commented out in ESP32
36.         "light_level": 0       # Not testing light sensor today - commented out in ESP32
37.     }
38.     
39.     print(f"\n{'='*60}")
40.     print(f"Sending soil moisture reading: {soil_moisture_value}%")
41.     print(f"URL: {url}")
42.     print(f"Payload: {payload}")
43.     print(f"{'='*60}")
44.     
45.     try:
46.         response = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)
47.         
48.         print(f"\nHTTP Status Code: {response.status_code}")
49.         
50.         if response.status_code == 200:
51.             print("✅ SUCCESS: Data sent to backend!")
52.             data = response.json()
53.             print(f"Backend response: {data}")
54.             return True
55.         else:
56.             print(f"⚠️  WARNING: Backend returned error code {response.status_code}")
57.             print(f"Response: {response.text}")
58.             return False
59.             
60.     except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
61.         print("❌ ERROR: Cannot connect to backend!")
62.         print("   Make sure the backend server is running:")
63.         print("   cd backend && source venv/bin/activate && uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000")
64.         return False
65.     except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
66.         print("❌ ERROR: Request timed out!")
67.         return False
68.     except Exception as e:
69.         print(f"❌ ERROR: {e}")
70.         return False
71. 
72. 
73. def main():
74.     print("\n" + "="*70)
75.     print(" AgriSense - ESP32 Data Flow Test (Soil Moisture Only)")
76.     print("="*70)
77.     print("\nThis script simulates ESP32 sending soil moisture data to backend.")
78.     print("ML prediction is COMMENTED OUT - only data storage is tested.")
79.     print("\nSimulating 5 readings with different moisture levels...")
80.     print("Press Ctrl+C to stop early.\n")
81.     
82.     # Simulate different soil moisture scenarios
83.     test_readings = [
84.         25,  # Dry - needs water
85.         45,  # Medium - okay
86.         70,  # Wet - good
87.         35,  # Getting dry
88.         60,  # After watering
89.     ]
90.     
91.     success_count = 0
92.     
93.     for i, moisture in enumerate(test_readings, 1):
94.         print(f"\n>>> Reading {i}/{len(test_readings)}")
95.         
96.         if send_soil_moisture_reading(moisture):
97.             success_count += 1
98.         
99.         if i < len(test_readings):
100.             print(f"Waiting 2 seconds (simulating ESP32 interval)...")
101.             time.sleep(2)
102.     
103.     print(f"\n{'='*70}")
104.     print(f"Test Complete: {success_count}/{len(test_readings)} readings sent successfully")
105.     print(f"{'='*70}\n")
106.     
107.     if success_count == len(test_readings):
108.         print("✅ All readings sent successfully!")
109.         print("\nNext steps:")
110.         print("1. Check Firebase Console to verify data is stored")
111.         print("2. Check frontend dashboard to see if values display")
112.         print("3. Verify NO ML predictions were triggered (commented out)")
113.     else:
114.         print("⚠️  Some readings failed. Check backend logs for details.")
115. 
116. 
117. if __name__ == "__main__":
118.     main()

28.         if firestore_user and not firestore_user.is_deleted:
29.             raise HTTPException(
30.                 status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
31.                 detail="Email already registered and active"
32.             )
33.         elif firestore_user and firestore_user.is_deleted:
34.             # User exists but is soft-deleted, allow re-registration
35.             fb_user_details = firebase_service.get_user_by_uid(existing_firebase_user.uid)
36.             if fb_user_details and fb_user_details.disabled:
37.                 firebase_service.enable_firebase_user(existing_firebase_user.uid)
38.             
39.             # Update existing firestore user and mark as not deleted

43.             # After reactivating, we should update their display name if provided and return them

46.

7. class UserBase(BaseModel):
8.     email: str

11.     full_name: Optional[str] = None
12.     dashboard_preferences: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None
13. 
14.     @field_validator('email')
15.     @classmethod
16.     def validate_email(cls, v: str) -> str:
17.         if not re.match(r"[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+", v):
18.             raise ValueError('Invalid email format')
19.         return v.lower()
20. 
21. 
22. class UserCreate(UserBase):
23.     password: str
24. 
25.     @field_validator('password')
26.     @classmethod
27.     def validate_password(cls, v: str) -> str:
28.         if len(v) < 8:
29.             raise ValueError('Password must be at least 8 characters long')
30.         if not re.search(r'[A-Z]', v):
31.             raise ValueError('Password must contain at least one uppercase letter')
32.         if not re.search(r'[a-z]', v):
33.             raise ValueError('Password must contain at least one lowercase letter')
34.         if not re.search(r'\d', v):
35.             raise ValueError('Password must contain at least one digit')
36.         if not re.search(r'[!@#$%^&*(),.?":{}|<>]', v):
37.             raise ValueError('Password must contain at least one special character')
38.         return v
39.

1. from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
2. from typing import Dict, Any, List

4. import pandas as pd

10. class MLService:
11.     """
12.     ML Service that loads a pre-trained model to make irrigation predictions.
13.     """
14.     
15.     def __init__(self):
16.         """
17.         Initializes the MLService by loading the trained model.
18.         The model is loaded using joblib from the /model directory.
19.         """
20.         # Construct the absolute path to the new model file in the /model directory
21.         base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
22.         model_path = os.path.join(base_dir, '..', '..', '..', 'model', 'irrigation_model.pkl')
23.         
24.         try:
25.             self.model = joblib.load(model_path)
26.             print(f"Successfully loaded model from {model_path}")
27.         except FileNotFoundError:
28.             print(f"Error: Model file not found at {model_path}")
29.             self.model = None
30.         except Exception as e:
31.             print(f"An error occurred while loading the model: {e}")
32.             self.model = None
33. 
34.     async def predict_irrigation_need(self, sensor_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
35.         """
36.         Predict irrigation valve duration based on sensor data using the loaded ML model.
37.         """
38.         if self.model is None:
39.             return {
40.                 "error": "The irrigation prediction model could not be loaded.",
41.                 "predicted_valve_duration_s": None,
42.                 "predicted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
43.                 "input_data": sensor_data,
44.             }
45. 
46.         # The model was trained with specific feature names. We must match them exactly.
47.         # These are the columns from the notebook:
48.         # ['Soil Moisture (%)', 'Temperature (°C)', 'Humidity (%)', 'Light Level (lx)']
49.         
50.         # Map API input keys to the required model feature names
51.         input_data_for_model = {
52.             'Soil Moisture (%)': sensor_data.get('soil_moisture'),
53.             'Temperature (°C)': sensor_data.get('temperature'),
54.             'Humidity (%)': sensor_data.get('humidity'),
55.             'Light Level (lx)': sensor_data.get('light_level')
56.         }
57. 
58.         # Check if all required data is present
59.         if any(value is None for value in input_data_for_model.values()):
60.             return {
61.                 "error": "Missing one or more required sensor data fields: soil_moisture, temperature, humidity, light_level.",
62.                 "predicted_valve_duration_s": None,
63.                 "input_data": sensor_data
64.             }
65.         
66.         try:
67.             # Create a DataFrame with the exact feature names the model was trained on
68.             input_df = pd.DataFrame([input_data_for_model])
69.             
70.             # Get prediction from the model
71.             predicted_duration = self.model.predict(input_df)[0]
72.             
73.             # The model predicts the valve duration in seconds.
74.             # We can add a simple floor to prevent negative predictions if the model were to do that.
75.             predicted_duration = max(0, predicted_duration)
76. 
77.         except Exception as e:
78.             return {
79.                 "error": f"Failed to get prediction: {e}",
80.                 "predicted_valve_duration_s": None,
81.                 "input_data": sensor_data
82.             }
83. 
84.         return {
85.             "predicted_valve_duration_s": round(predicted_duration, 2),
86.             "unit": "seconds",
87.             "predicted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
88.             "input_data": sensor_data
89.         }
90.     
91.     async def predict_future_irrigation_needs(self, device_id: str, hours_ahead: int = 48) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
92.         """
93.         Predict irrigation needs for future hours based on simulated sensor data.
94.         """
95.         future_predictions = []
96.         current_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
97. 
98.         # Get the latest actual sensor reading as a starting point
99.         latest_actual_reading = await sensor_service.get_latest_sensor_reading(device_id)
100. 
101.         if not latest_actual_reading:
102.             print(f"WARNING: No latest sensor reading found for device {device_id}. Cannot predict future.")
103.             return []
104. 
105.         # Initialize simulated sensor values with the latest actual reading (with defaults)
106.         simulated_soil_moisture = latest_actual_reading.soil_moisture if latest_actual_reading.soil_moisture is not None else 30.0
107.         simulated_temperature = latest_actual_reading.temperature if latest_actual_reading.temperature is not None else 25.0
108.         simulated_humidity = latest_actual_reading.humidity if latest_actual_reading.humidity is not None else 50.0
109.         simulated_light_level = latest_actual_reading.light_level if latest_actual_reading.light_level is not None else 500.0
110. 
111.         for i in range(1, hours_ahead + 1):
112.             future_time = current_time + timedelta(hours=i)
113. 
114.             # Simple simulation: random walk with bounds
115.             # Keep values within reasonable ranges (e.g., soil moisture 0-100, temp -10-50, humidity 0-100, light 0-2000)
116.             simulated_soil_moisture = max(0.0, min(100.0, simulated_soil_moisture + random.uniform(-2.0, 2.0)))
117.             simulated_temperature = max(-10.0, min(50.0, simulated_temperature + random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)))
118.             simulated_humidity = max(0.0, min(100.0, simulated_humidity + random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)))
119.             
120.             # Light level can vary more significantly with day/night cycles, but for simplicity, a random walk for now
121.             # A more advanced simulation would consider time of day.
122.             simulated_light_level = max(0.0, min(2000.0, simulated_light_level + random.uniform(-50.0, 50.0)))
123. 
124. 
125.             simulated_sensor_data = {
126.                 'soil_moisture': simulated_soil_moisture,
127.                 'temperature': simulated_temperature,
128.                 'humidity': simulated_humidity,
129.                 'light_level': simulated_light_level
130.             }
131. 
132.             prediction_result = await self.predict_irrigation_need(simulated_sensor_data)
133.             
134.             future_predictions.append({
135.                 "predicted_at": future_time.isoformat(),
136.                 "predicted_valve_duration_s": prediction_result["predicted_valve_duration_s"],
137.                 "input_data": simulated_sensor_data
138.             })
139.         
140.         return future_predictions
141.

9. def train_and_save_model():
10.     """
11.     This script trains a RandomForestRegressor model on the system_data.csv
12.     and saves the trained model to a new file, 'irrigation_model.pkl',
13.     in the same directory as the script.
14.     """
15.     # --- 1. Load Data ---
16.     # Construct the path to the CSV file relative to this script's location
17.     try:
18.         script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
19.         csv_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'system_data.csv')
20.         df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
21.         print("Successfully loaded system_data.csv")
22.     except FileNotFoundError:
23.         print(f"Error: system_data.csv not found at {csv_path}")
24.         return
25. 
26.     # --- 2. Define Features (X) and Target (y) ---
27.     # Ensure column names match the CSV file exactly
28.     features = ['Soil Moisture (%)', 'Temperature (°C)', 'Humidity (%)', 'Light Level (lx)']
29.     target = 'Valve Duration (s)'
30. 
31.     X = df[features]
32.     y = df[target]
33.     print("Features and target defined.")
34. 
35.     # --- 3. Split Data ---
36.     X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
37.         X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
38.     )
39.     print("Data split into training and testing sets.")
40. 
41.     # --- 4. Train the Model ---
42.     # Using the RandomForestRegressor as specified in the notebook
43.     model = RandomForestRegressor(
44.         n_estimators=100,
45.         random_state=42
46.     )
47.     print("Training the RandomForestRegressor model...")
48.     model.fit(X_train, y_train)
49.     print("Model training complete.")
50. 
51.     # --- 5. Evaluate the Model (Optional but good practice) ---
52.     y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
53.     r2 = r2_score(y_test, y_pred)
54.     print(f"Model evaluation (R2 Score): {r2:.4f}")
55. 
56.     # --- 6. Save the Trained Model ---
57.     # Save the new model to 'irrigation_model.pkl' in the same directory
58.     model_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'irrigation_model.pkl')
59.     joblib.dump(model, model_path)
60.     
61.     print("-" * 50)
62.     print(f"Successfully trained and saved new model to:")

64.     print("-" * 50)
65.

96.         }
97.

99.         await asyncio.to_thread(doc_ref.update, update_data)
100.

102.         return IrrigationEvent(**updated_event_doc.to_dict())

40. The backend will be available at `http://localhost:8000`.
41. 
42. ## Frontend Setup
43. 
44. ### 1. Environment Setup
45. 
46. ```bash
47. # Navigate to the frontend directory
48. cd /path/to/agrisense/Frontend
49. 
50. # Install dependencies
51. npm install
52. ```
53. 
54. ### 2. Frontend Configuration
55. 
56. The frontend is configured to connect to the backend API. You can customize the API base URL in `src/config.js`:
57. 
58. ```javascript
59. API_BASE_URL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL || "http://localhost:8000/api/v1"
60. ```
61. 
62. ### 3. Starting the Frontend
63. 
64. ```bash
65. cd /path/to/agrisense/Frontend
66. npm run dev
67. ```
68. 
69. The frontend will be available at `http://localhost:5173` (or similar available port).
70. 
71. ## Connection Flow
72. 
73. 1. **Authentication**: The frontend communicates with `/auth/login` and `/auth/register` endpoints
74. 2. **Data Retrieval**: The frontend fetches sensor data, alerts, and irrigation logs from respective backend endpoints
75. 3. **Control Commands**: The frontend sends irrigation commands to the backend
76. 4. **Fallback Mechanism**: If the backend is unavailable, the frontend falls back to mock data services
77. 
78. ## Development Features
79. 
80. ### Mock Data Services
81. - When the backend is unavailable, the frontend automatically uses mock data
82. - Mock data includes devices, sensor readings, irrigation events, and alerts
83. - Mock authentication generates temporary tokens
84. 
85. ### API Service Enhancements
86. - Automatic fallback to mock services when backend is unreachable
87. - Proper error handling and user notifications
88. - Consistent data format between real and mock services
89. 
90. ## Testing the Connection
91. 
92. 1. Start the backend server
93. 2. Start the frontend server
94. 3. Access the frontend in your browser
95. 4. Register a new user or use existing credentials
96. 5. Verify that data loads and displays correctly
97. 6. Test irrigation controls to ensure they communicate with the backend
98. 
99. ## Troubleshooting
100. 
101. ### Common Issues
102. 
103. - **Port Already in Use**: The frontend may start on a different port (e.g., 5174 instead of 5173)
104. - **Backend Unavailable**: The frontend will automatically switch to mock data
105. - **Firebase Errors**: The backend uses mock Firebase services when credentials are not provided
106. 
107. ### Verification Steps
108. 
109. 1. Check if backend is running: `curl http://localhost:8000/health`
110. 2. Check if frontend is running: Access the URL shown in the terminal

```
1. # AgriSense Copilot Instructions
2. 
3. ## Build, test, and lint commands
4. 
5. ### Frontend (`Frontend/`)
6. - Install deps: `npm install`
7. - Run dev server: `npm run dev`
8. - Production build: `npm run build`
9. - Preview build: `npm run preview`
10. 
11. ### Backend (`backend/`)
12. - Setup env and deps:
13.   - `python -m venv venv`
14.   - `source venv/bin/activate`
15.   - `pip install -r requirements.txt`
16. - Start API (project-standard entrypoint): `python start_server.py`
17.   - Optional simulator mode: `USE_SIMULATOR=true python start_server.py`
18. - Run tests: `pytest -q`
19. - Run a single test: `pytest -q test_user_management.py::test_register_user`
20. 
21. ### Linting
22. - No repository lint command is currently configured in `package.json` or backend project files.
23. 
24. ## High-level architecture
25. 
26. - **Frontend (Vue 3 + Vite)** in `Frontend/src` uses a service/store split:
27.   - `services/auth.js` owns Firebase Auth state transitions.
28.   - `services/api.js` is the single backend client and injects bearer tokens on every request.
29.   - `store/auth.js` stores `authStore.user` and `accessToken`.
30.   - `router.js` enforces `requiresAuth` and role-based route guards via `meta.roles`.
31. 
32. - **Backend (FastAPI)** in `backend/app` is route/service layered:
33.   - `main.py` registers routers by domain (`/auth`, `/users`, `/sensors`, `/irrigation`, `/alerts`, etc.).
34.   - `middleware/auth.py` (`JWTBearer`) verifies bearer tokens and writes decoded claims to `request.state.user`.
35.   - Route modules handle HTTP validation/authorization and delegate Firestore logic to `services/*`.
36.   - Services consistently wrap blocking Firestore SDK calls in `asyncio.to_thread(...)`.
37. 
38. - **Data/auth flow**:
39.   - Frontend signs users in with Firebase SDK, then sends Firebase ID tokens to FastAPI in `Authorization: Bearer ...`.
40.   - Backend validates Firebase tokens against Google public keys (`services/auth_service.py`) and uses Firestore for app data.
41.   - If Firebase Admin credentials are missing, backend falls back to mock Firebase/Firestore (`services/firebase_service.py`) and seeds a default admin user plus `esp32-b47cb8` device.
42. 
43. - **ML component**:
44.   - Model training script is `model/train_model.py` and outputs `model/irrigation_model.pkl`.
45.   - Backend `ml_service.py` can load the model, but production-facing ML endpoints in `routes/ml.py` are mostly disabled/commented; only `/ml/status` is active.
46. 
47. ## Key conventions in this repository
48. 
49. - **Initialize Firebase before app mount**: frontend startup in `src/main.js` calls `firebaseService.initialize()` before registering auth listeners and mounting Vue.
50. 
51. - **Token freshness is forced**: frontend auth/API flows call `currentUser.getIdToken(true)` (forced refresh), not stale cached JWT assumptions.
52. 
53. - **Auth race avoidance pattern**: API requests wait on `firebaseAuthReadyPromise` (from `services/auth.js`) before issuing authenticated backend requests.
54. 
55. - **Local auth token key is fixed**: frontend persists token under `localStorage["accessToken"]`; reuse this exact key.
56. 
57. - **Backend identity source is request state**: protected routes read identity from `request.state.user` populated by `JWTBearer`, instead of reparsing headers in each route.
58. 
59. - **Mock-first backend fallback is intentional**: missing Firebase credentials should not block development; backend automatically switches to mock services.
60. 
61. - **Current dashboard/device assumption**: frontend dashboard currently prefers device `esp32-b47cb8` and falls back to it when device discovery fails.
62. 
63. - **Irrigation ML path is intentionally stubbed right now**: frontend API methods `getMLPrediction` / `getIrrigationPredictions` return disabled/dummy responses aligned with backend ML route status.
64.
```

</details>

130.   } else {
131.     soilSensorConnected = false;
132.     Serial.println("[--] Soil Moisture Sensor: NOT CONNECTED");
133.   }
134. 
135.   // DHT22
136.   dht.begin();
137.   delay(2000);
138.   float testHumidity    = dht.readHumidity();
139.   float testTemperature = dht.readTemperature();
140.   if (!isnan(testHumidity) && !isnan(testTemperature)) {
141.     dhtSensorConnected = true;
142.     Serial.println("[OK] DHT22 Sensor: CONNECTED");
143.   } else {
144.     dhtSensorConnected = false;
145.     Serial.println("[--] DHT22 Sensor: NOT CONNECTED");
146.   }
147. 
148.   // BH1750
149.   Wire.begin(I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL);
150.   if (lightMeter.begin(BH1750::CONTINUOUS_HIGH_RES_MODE)) {
151.     delay(200);
152.     float testLight = lightMeter.readLightLevel();
153.     if (testLight >= 0) {
154.       lightSensorConnected = true;
155.       Serial.println("[OK] BH1750 Light Sensor: CONNECTED");
156.     } else {
157.       lightSensorConnected = false;
158.       Serial.println("[--] BH1750 Light Sensor: NOT CONNECTED");
159.     }
160.   } else {
161.     lightSensorConnected = false;
162.     Serial.println("[--] BH1750 Light Sensor: NOT CONNECTED");
163.   }
164. 
165.   Serial.println("-------------------------\n");
166. }
167. 
168. // =============================================================================
169. // Read Sensors
170. // =============================================================================
171. void readSensors() {
172.   // Soil Moisture
173.   if (soilSensorConnected) {
174.     int rawValue   = analogRead(SOIL_MOISTURE_PIN);
175.     int percentage = map(rawValue, SOIL_MOISTURE_DRY, SOIL_MOISTURE_WET, 0, 100);
176.     soilMoisture   = (float)constrain(percentage, 0, 100);
177.   } else {
178.     soilMoisture = NAN;
179.   }
180. 
181.   // DHT22
182.   if (dhtSensorConnected) {
183.     float h = dht.readHumidity();
184.     float t = dht.readTemperature();
185.     if (!isnan(h) && !isnan(t)) {
186.       humidity    = h;
187.       temperature = t;
188.     } else {
189.       humidity    = NAN;
190.       temperature = NAN;
191.       Serial.println("WARNING: DHT22 lost connection!");
192.     }
193.   } else {
194.     humidity    = NAN;
195.     temperature = NAN;
196.   }
197. 
198.   // BH1750
199.   if (lightSensorConnected) {
200.     float lux = lightMeter.readLightLevel();
201.     if (lux >= 0) {
202.       lightLevel = lux;
203.     } else {
204.       lightLevel = NAN;
205.       Serial.println("WARNING: BH1750 lost connection!");
206.     }
207.   } else {
208.     lightLevel = NAN;
209.   }
210. }
211. 
212. // =============================================================================
213. // Print Sensor Status
214. // =============================================================================
215. void printSensorStatus() {
216.   Serial.println("--- Sensor Readings ---");
217. 
218.   Serial.print("Soil Moisture : ");
219.   Serial.println(!isnan(soilMoisture) ? String(soilMoisture) + "%" : "OFFLINE");
220. 
221.   Serial.print("Temperature   : ");
222.   Serial.println(!isnan(temperature) ? String(temperature) + "C" : "OFFLINE");
223. 
224.   Serial.print("Humidity      : ");
225.   Serial.println(!isnan(humidity) ? String(humidity) + "%" : "OFFLINE");
226. 
227.   Serial.print("Light Level   : ");
228.   Serial.println(!isnan(lightLevel) ? String(lightLevel) + " lux" : "OFFLINE");
229. 
230.   Serial.println("-----------------------");
231. }
232. 
233. // =============================================================================
234. // Float or Null (send null for disconnected sensors)
235. // =============================================================================
236. String floatOrNull(float value) {
237.   if (isnan(value)) return "null";
238.   return String(value, 2);
239. }
240. 
241. // =============================================================================
242. // Send Data to Backend
243. // =============================================================================
244. void sendDataToBackend() {
245.   if (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) {
246.     Serial.println("WARNING: WiFi disconnected, skipping send.");
247.     return;
248.   }
249. 
250.   HTTPClient http;
251.   String apiUrl = String(API_BASE_URL) + "/sensors/" + deviceId + "/readings";
252. 
253.   http.begin(apiUrl);
254.   http.addHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");
255. 
256.   String jsonPayload = "{";
257.   jsonPayload += "\"device_id\":\""   + deviceId              + "\",";
258.   jsonPayload += "\"soil_moisture\":" + floatOrNull(soilMoisture) + ",";
259.   jsonPayload += "\"temperature\":"   + floatOrNull(temperature)  + ",";
260.   jsonPayload += "\"humidity\":"      + floatOrNull(humidity)     + ",";
261.   jsonPayload += "\"light_level\":"   + floatOrNull(lightLevel);
262.   jsonPayload += "}";
263. 
264.   Serial.print("Sending: ");
265.   Serial.println(jsonPayload);
266. 
267.   int httpResponseCode = http.POST(jsonPayload);
268.   Serial.print("Response: ");
269.   Serial.println(httpResponseCode);
270.   http.end();
271. }
272. 
273. // =============================================================================
274. // Poll Control State
275. // =============================================================================
276. void pollControlState() {
277.   if (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) return;
278. 
279.   HTTPClient http;
280.   String url = String(API_BASE_URL) + "/irrigation/control/" + deviceId;
281.   http.begin(url);
282.   int httpResponseCode = http.GET();
283. 
284.   if (httpResponseCode == 200) {
285.     String payload = http.getString();
286.     JsonDocument doc;
287.     deserializeJson(doc, payload);
288.     bool pumpState = doc["pump_state"];
289. 
290.     Serial.print("Pump state from backend: ");
291.     Serial.println(pumpState ? "ON" : "OFF");
292. 
293.     // Active-LOW relay: LOW = ON, HIGH = OFF
294.     digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, pumpState ? LOW : HIGH);
295.     
296.     Serial.print("Relay signal sent: ");
297.     Serial.println(pumpState ? "LOW (Pump ON)" : "HIGH (Pump OFF)");
298.   } else {
299.     Serial.print("Control state fetch failed: ");
300.     Serial.println(httpResponseCode);
301.   }
302.   http.end();
303. }
304. 
305. // =============================================================================
306. // Setup
307. // =============================================================================
308. void setup() {
309.   Serial.begin(115200);
310.   pinMode(RELAY_PIN, OUTPUT);
311.   
312.   // Relay hardware test - runs on boot
313.   Serial.println("\n--- Testing Relay Hardware ---");
314.   Serial.println("Relay ON (Signal: LOW)...");
315.   digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, LOW);   
316.   delay(2000);
317.   Serial.println("Relay OFF (Signal: HIGH)...");
318.   digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, HIGH);  
319.   delay(2000);
320.   Serial.println("Relay test done.\n");
321. 
322.   delay(1000);
323.   Serial.println("=== AgriSense Starting ===");
324.   setupWifi();
325.   generateDeviceId();
326.   detectSensors();
327. }
328. 
329. // =============================================================================
330. // Loop
331. // =============================================================================
332. void loop() {
333.   unsigned long currentMillis = millis();
334.   if (currentMillis - lastReadTime >= SENSOR_READ_INTERVAL_MS) {
335.     lastReadTime = currentMillis;
336.     readSensors();
337.     printSensorStatus();
338.     sendDataToBackend();
339.     pollControlState();
340.   }
341. }
342.
```

53.     async def create_sensor_reading(self, device_id: str, reading_create: SensorReadingCreate) -> SensorReading:
54.         now = time.time()
55.         sensor_reading_id = f"reading_{datetime.utcnow().timestamp()}"
56.         new_reading = SensorReading(
57.             id=sensor_reading_id,
58.             device_id=device_id,

60.             temperature=reading_create.temperature,

62.             light_level=reading_create.light_level,
63.             timestamp=reading_create.timestamp or datetime.utcnow()
64.         )
65.         
66.         # Update in-memory cache IMMEDIATELY (for live dashboard)
67.         self._latest_sensor_data_cache[device_id] = new_reading
68. 
69.         # Only save to Firestore if the interval has passed (periodic backup)
70.         last_save = self._last_firestore_save.get(device_id, 0)
71.         if now - last_save >= self.FIRESTORE_SAVE_INTERVAL:
72.             try:
73.                 doc_ref = self.db.collection('sensor_readings').document(sensor_reading_id)
74.                 await asyncio.to_thread(doc_ref.set, new_reading.model_dump())
75.                 self._last_firestore_save[device_id] = now
76.                 print(f"✅ [SensorService] Periodic Firestore backup for {device_id} successful.")
77.             except Exception as e:
78.                 print(f"❌ [SensorService] Firestore backup failed for {device_id}: {e}")
79.         else:

81.             pass
82.         
83.         return new_reading

85.     async def get_latest_sensor_reading(self, device_id: str) -> Optional[SensorReading]:

94.             .order_by('timestamp', direction=firestore.Query.DESCENDING)
95.             .limit(1)

99.         if readings:
100.             latest_reading = SensorReading(**readings[0].to_dict())

102.             return latest_reading
103.         return None

237.             }

240. 
241.     async def simulate_irrigation_effect(self, device_id: str, duration_seconds: int) -> Optional[SensorReading]:
242.         # Fetch the latest reading to base the simulation on
243.         latest_reading = await self.get_latest_sensor_reading(device_id)
244.         
245.         if not latest_reading:
246.             print(f"WARNING: Cannot simulate irrigation effect for device {device_id}: no latest reading found.")
247.             return None
248.         
249.         # Calculate soil moisture increase: example 5-8% increase per 120s (2 minutes)
250.         # So, per second: (5-8)% / 120 = 0.041-0.066%
251.         increase_per_second = random.uniform(0.041, 0.066)
252.         
253.         current_moisture = latest_reading.soil_moisture if latest_reading.soil_moisture is not None else 30.0
254.         simulated_moisture_increase = increase_per_second * duration_seconds
255.         
256.         new_soil_moisture = min(100.0, current_moisture + simulated_moisture_increase)
257.         
258.         # Other values can be slightly randomized or kept the same
259.         new_temperature = round((latest_reading.temperature or 25.0) + random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0), 2)
260.         new_humidity = round((latest_reading.humidity or 50.0) + random.uniform(-2.0, 2.0), 2)
261.         new_light_level = round((latest_reading.light_level or 500.0) + random.uniform(-10.0, 10.0), 2)
262. 
263.         simulated_reading_create = SensorReadingCreate(
264.             device_id=device_id,
265.             soil_moisture=new_soil_moisture,
266.             temperature=new_temperature,
267.             humidity=new_humidity,
268.             light_level=new_light_level,
269.             timestamp=datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=1) # Slightly after the event for distinct timestamp
270.         )
271.         
272.         print(f"Simulating irrigation effect for device {device_id}: moisture increased from {current_moisture:.2f}% to {new_soil_moisture:.2f}% over {duration_seconds} seconds.")
273.         return await self.create_sensor_reading(device_id, simulated_reading_create)
274. 
275. 
276. # Initialize the service
277. sensor_service = SensorService()
278.

174.   String jsonPayload = "{";
175.   jsonPayload += "\"device_id\":\""   + deviceId + "\",";
176.   jsonPayload += "\"soil_moisture\":" + String(soilMoisture, 2) + ",";
177.   jsonPayload += "\"temperature\":"   + String(temperature, 2) + ",";  // Updated to real value
178.   jsonPayload += "\"humidity\":"      + String(humidity, 2) + ",";     // Updated to real value
179.   jsonPayload += "\"light_level\":"   + String(lightLevel, 2);         // Updated to real value
180.   jsonPayload += "}";
181. 
182.   Serial.print("Payload: ");
183.   Serial.println(jsonPayload);
184. 
185.   int httpResponseCode = http.POST(jsonPayload);
186. 
187.   if (httpResponseCode > 0) {
188.     Serial.print("HTTP Response: ");

190.     if (httpResponseCode == 200 || httpResponseCode == 201) {
191.       Serial.println("✅ Data sent successfully!");
192.     }
193.   } else {

195.     Serial.println(http.errorToString(httpResponseCode).c_str());
196.   }
197. 
198.   http.end();
199. }

201. void setup() {
202.   Serial.begin(115200);
203. 
204.   // Initialize DHT sensor
205.   dht.begin();
206. 
207.   // Initialize BH1750 sensor
208.   if (lightMeter.begin()) {
209.     Serial.println("BH1750 sensor initialized successfully!");
210.   } else {
211.     Serial.println("Error: Unable to initialize BH1750 sensor!");
212.   }
213. 
214.   // Initialize relay
215.   setupRelay();
216. 
217.   generateDeviceId();
218.   setupWifi();
219. }
220. 
221. void loop() {
222.   unsigned long currentTime = millis();
223.   if (currentTime - lastReadTime >= SENSOR_READ_INTERVAL_MS) {
224.     lastReadTime = currentTime;
225. 
226.     // Read all sensors
227.     soilMoisture = readSoilMoisture();
228.     bool dhtSuccess = readDHT22();
229.     bool bh1750Success = readBH1750();
230. 
231.     if(dhtSuccess && bh1750Success) {
232.       // Basic irrigation logic: if soil moisture is below threshold, turn on relay
233.       const float MOISTURE_THRESHOLD = 30.0; // Turn on irrigation if soil moisture is below 30%
234. 
235.       if(soilMoisture < MOISTURE_THRESHOLD) {
236.         controlRelay(true);  // Turn ON irrigation
237.       } else {
238.         controlRelay(false); // Turn OFF irrigation
239.       }
240. 
241.       printReadings();
242.       sendDataToBackend();
243.     } else {
244.       if(!dhtSuccess) {
245.         Serial.println("Skipping data send due to DHT read failure");
246.       }
247.       if(!bh1750Success) {
248.         Serial.println("Skipping data send due to BH1750 read failure");
249.       }
250.     }
251.   }
252. }

85.   Serial.print("Payload: ");
86.   Serial.println(jsonPayload);
87. 
88.   int httpResponseCode = http.POST(jsonPayload);
89. 
90.   if (httpResponseCode > 0) {
91.     Serial.print("HTTP Response: ");
92.     Serial.println(httpResponseCode);
93.     if (httpResponseCode == 200 || httpResponseCode == 201) {
94.       Serial.println("✅ Data sent successfully!");
95.     }
96.   } else {
97.     Serial.print("❌ Error: ");
98.     Serial.println(http.errorToString(httpResponseCode).c_str());
99.   }
100. 
101.   http.end();
102. }
103. 
104. void setup() {
105.   Serial.begin(115200);
106.   generateDeviceId();
107.   setupWifi();
108. }
109. 
110. void loop() {
111.   unsigned long currentTime = millis();
112.   if (currentTime - lastReadTime >= SENSOR_READ_INTERVAL_MS) {
113.     lastReadTime = currentTime;
114.     soilMoisture = readSoilMoisture();
115.     printReadings();
116.     sendDataToBackend();
117.   }
118. }

### 💬 Copilot

Correct — `AgriSense_ESP32.ino` is the hardware control file, and your symptoms are consistent with a hardware/control-sync issue there plus control-state behavior.

I’ve already adjusted it so the ESP32 now boots with pump **OFF** (no startup relay pulse) and uses a single relay-mapping function (`RELAY_ACTIVE_LOW`) for correct ON/OFF signaling. I also fixed frontend control-state error handling (so dashboard won’t claim success if control update fails) and normalized backend auto-threshold behavior (legacy low defaults won’t block AUTO start).

What this means for your exact issue:
1. **“Dashboard says started, pump didn’t”**: UI was optimistic and relay logic/polarity could be mismatched.
2. **“Pump starts briefly on power cut/restart”**: startup relay toggling/unsafe boot state was the cause.
3. **“AUTO not starting”**: AUTO only works when mode is truly `AUTO` and moisture is below threshold; older threshold defaults could be too low.

Apply these now:
1. Reflash ESP32 with the updated `AgriSense_ESP32.ino`.
2. Ensure relay wiring uses **COM + NO** (not NC).
3. If your relay board is active-HIGH, set `RELAY_ACTIVE_LOW = false`.
4. In dashboard, set mode to **Auto** and confirm moisture readings are still being posted every ~2s.

<sub>⏱️ 22m 41s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Your wiring is the main issue: the pump is on **NC (常闭)**, so behavior is inverted.

1. **Label meaning**
- **常开** = NO (Normally Open)
- **公共端** = COM
- **常闭** = NC (Normally Closed)

2. **Your current wiring**
- COM → power supply red (+)
- NC → pump red (+)
- NO empty

That makes pump powered in the relay’s default/off state, which explains the strange “starts briefly on stop/power cut” behavior.

3. **Correct wiring for normal irrigation control**
- COM (**公共端**) → power supply red (+)
- NO (**常开**) → pump red (+)  **(move pump wire here)**
- NC (**常闭**) → leave empty
- Pump black (−) and power black (−) together (this part is fine)

4. **Flyback diode**
Your diode direction is correct for DC load:
- Stripe side (cathode) → pump red (+)
- Non-stripe side → pump black (−)

If ON/OFF still looks reversed after rewiring, flip `RELAY_ACTIVE_LOW` in `AgriSense_ESP32.ino` (`true` ↔ `false`).

84. const getChartData = () => {
85.   const predictions = predictionData.value;
86.   const userPrefs = authStore.user?.preferences || {
87.     temperature_unit: 'Celsius',
88.     volume_unit: 'liters',
89.     time_zone: 'UTC',
90.     notification_sound: 'default'
91.   };
92.   
93.   const volumeUnit = formatWithUserPreferences(0, 'volume', userPrefs).unit;
94. 
95.   if (!predictions || predictions.length === 0) {
96.     return {
97.       labels: [],
98.       datasets: [{
99.         label: `Valve Duration (${volumeUnit})`,
100.         data: [],
101.         backgroundColor: 'rgba(200, 200, 200, 0.6)',
102.         borderColor: 'rgba(200, 200, 200, 1)',
103.         borderWidth: 1,
104.       }]
105.     };
106.   }
107. 
108.   // Generate labels for each hour, including date
109.   const labels = predictions.map(p => {

111.     // Format to a readable date and time, e.g., "Feb 19, 6:00 PM"
112.     return date.toLocaleDateString([], { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' });
113.   });
114. 
115.   // Extract predicted valve durations
116.   const data = predictions.map(p => p.predicted_valve_duration_s / 60);
117. 
118.   return {
119.     labels: labels,
120.     datasets: [{
121.       label: `Valve Duration (${volumeUnit})`,
122.       data: data,
123.       backgroundColor: 'rgba(54, 162, 235, 0.6)',
124.       borderColor: 'rgba(54, 162, 235, 1)',
125.       borderWidth: 1,
126.       fill: false, // For line chart
127.       tension: 0.1 // For smooth lines
128.     }]

130. };

138.     time_zone: 'UTC',
139.     notification_sound: 'default'
140.   };
141.   chartInstance.value = new Chart(ctx, {
142.     type: 'line', // Changed to line chart type for future predictions
143.     data: getChartData(),

153.                 },

158.                     }

160.                 }
161.             }

163.       },

168.           ticks: { maxRotation: 45, autoSkip: true } // Rotate labels for better readability
169.         },
170.         y: {
171.           beginAtZero: true,
172.           title: { display: true, text: 'Valve Duration (minutes)' }
173.         }
174.       }
175.     }
176.   });
177. };
178. 
179. const updateChart = () => {
180.   if (chartInstance.value) {
181.     const newChartData = getChartData();
182.     chartInstance.value.data.labels = newChartData.labels;
183.     chartInstance.value.data.datasets[0].data = newChartData.datasets[0].data;
184.     chartInstance.value.data.datasets[0].backgroundColor = newChartData.datasets[0].backgroundColor;
185.     chartInstance.value.data.datasets[0].borderColor = newChartData.datasets[0].borderColor;
186.     chartInstance.value.options.scales.y.title.text = 'Valve Duration (minutes)';
187.

189.     if (chartInstance.value.config.type !== 'line') {
190.       chartInstance.value.config.type = 'line';
191.     }
192.     
193.     chartInstance.value.update();
194.   }
195. };

I set `ML_FEATURES_ENABLED = false` and gated ML paths in:

This leaves irrigation control focused on manual/auto pump control logic only. Restart the frontend (`cd Frontend && npm run dev`) to apply it.

# GitHub Copilot CLI Documentation

## README
# GitHub Copilot CLI

The power of GitHub Copilot, now in your terminal.

GitHub Copilot CLI brings AI-powered coding assistance directly to your command line, enabling you to build, debug, and understand code through natural language conversations. Powered by the same agentic harness as GitHub's Copilot coding agent, it provides intelligent assistance while staying deeply integrated with your GitHub workflow.

See [our official documentation](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/agents/about-copilot-cli) for more information.

![Image of the splash screen for the Copilot CLI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f40aa23d-09dd-499e-9457-1d57d3368887)


## 🚀 Introduction and Overview

We're bringing the power of GitHub Copilot coding agent directly to your terminal. With GitHub Copilot CLI, you can work locally and synchronously with an AI agent that understands your code and GitHub context.

- **Terminal-native development:** Work with Copilot coding agent directly in your command line — no context switching required.
- **GitHub integration out of the box:** Access your repositories, issues, and pull requests using natural language, all authenticated with your existing GitHub account.
- **Agentic capabilities:** Build, edit, debug, and refactor code with an AI collaborator that can plan and execute complex tasks.
- **MCP-powered extensibility:** Take advantage of the fact that the coding agent ships with GitHub's MCP server by default and supports custom MCP servers to extend capabilities.
- **Full control:** Preview every action before execution — nothing happens without your explicit approval.

We're still early in our journey, but with your feedback, we're rapidly iterating to make the GitHub Copilot CLI the best possible companion in your terminal.

## 📦 Getting Started

### Supported Platforms

- **Linux**
- **macOS**
- **Windows**

### Prerequisites

- (On Windows) **PowerShell** v6 or higher
- An **active Copilot subscription**. See [Copilot plans](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans?ref_cta=Copilot+plans+signup&ref_loc=install-copilot-cli&ref_page=docs).

If you have access to GitHub Copilot via your organization or enterprise, you cannot use GitHub Copilot CLI if your organization owner or enterprise administrator has disabled it in the organization or enterprise settings. See [Managing policies and features for GitHub Copilot in your organization](http://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/managing-github-copilot-in-your-organization/managing-github-copilot-features-in-your-organization/managing-policies-for-copilot-in-your-organization) for more information.

### Installation

Install with the install script (macOS and Linux):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | bash
```

Or

```bash
wget -qO- https://gh.io/copilot-install | bash
```

Use `| sudo bash` to run as root and install to `/usr/local/bin`.

Set `PREFIX` to install to `$PREFIX/bin/` directory. Defaults to `/usr/local`
when run as root or `$HOME/.local` when run as a non-root user.

Set `VERSION` to install a specific version. Defaults to the latest version.

For example, to install version `v0.0.369` to a custom directory:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | VERSION="v0.0.369" PREFIX="$HOME/custom" bash
```

Install with [Homebrew](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/copilot-cli) (macOS and Linux):

```bash
brew install copilot-cli
```

```bash
brew install copilot-cli@prerelease
```


Install with [WinGet](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli) (Windows):

```bash
winget install GitHub.Copilot
```

```bash
winget install GitHub.Copilot.Prerelease
```


Install with [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot) (macOS, Linux, and Windows):

```bash
npm install -g @github/copilot
```

```bash
npm install -g @github/copilot@prerelease
```


### Launching the CLI

```bash
copilot
```

On first launch, you'll be greeted with our adorable animated banner! If you'd like to see this banner again, launch `copilot` with the `--banner` flag.

If you're not currently logged in to GitHub, you'll be prompted to use the `/login` slash command. Enter this command and follow the on-screen instructions to authenticate.

#### Authenticate with a Personal Access Token (PAT)

You can also authenticate using a fine-grained PAT with the "Copilot Requests" permission enabled.

1. Visit https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
2. Under "Permissions," click "add permissions" and select "Copilot Requests"
3. Generate your token
4. Add the token to your environment via the environment variable `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` (in order of precedence)

### Using the CLI

Launch `copilot` in a folder that contains code you want to work with.

By default, `copilot` utilizes Claude Sonnet 4.5. Run the `/model` slash command to choose from other available models, including Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-5.

### Experimental Mode

Experimental mode enables access to new features that are still in development. You can activate experimental mode by:

- Launching with the `--experimental` flag: `copilot --experimental`
- Using the `/experimental` slash command from within the CLI

Once activated, the setting is persisted in your config, so the `--experimental` flag is no longer needed on subsequent launches.

#### Experimental Features

- **Autopilot mode:** Autopilot is a new mode (press `Shift+Tab` to cycle through modes), which encourages the agent to continue working until a task is completed.

Each time you submit a prompt to GitHub Copilot CLI, your monthly quota of premium requests is reduced by one. For information about premium requests, see [About premium requests](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/monitoring-usage-and-entitlements/about-premium-requests).

For more information about how to use the GitHub Copilot CLI, see [our official documentation](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/agents/about-copilot-cli).

## 🔧 Configuring LSP Servers

GitHub Copilot CLI supports Language Server Protocol (LSP) for enhanced code intelligence. This feature provides intelligent code features like go-to-definition, hover information, and diagnostics.

### Installing Language Servers

Copilot CLI does not bundle LSP servers. You need to install them separately. For example, to set up TypeScript support:

```bash
npm install -g typescript-language-server
```

For other languages, install the corresponding LSP server and configure it following the same pattern shown below.

### Configuring LSP Servers

LSP servers are configured through a dedicated LSP configuration file. You can configure LSP servers at the user level or repository level:

**User-level configuration** (applies to all projects):
Edit `~/.copilot/lsp-config.json`

**Repository-level configuration** (applies to specific project):
Create `.github/lsp.json` in your repository root

Example configuration:

```json
{
  "lspServers": {
    "typescript": {
      "command": "typescript-language-server",
      "args": ["--stdio"],
      "fileExtensions": {
        ".ts": "typescript",
        ".tsx": "typescript"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Viewing LSP Server Status

Check configured LSP servers using the `/lsp` command in an interactive session, or view your configuration files directly.

For more information, see the [changelog](./changelog.md).

## 📢 Feedback and Participation

We're excited to have you join us early in the Copilot CLI journey.

We're building quickly. Expect frequent updates--please keep your client up to date for the latest features and fixes!

Your insights are invaluable! Open an issue in this repo, join Discussions, and run `/feedback` from the CLI to submit a confidential feedback survey!

Global

Editing

  ctrl+e - move to end of line (when typing)

  ctrl+k - delete from cursor to end of line (joins lines at end of line)
  meta+← → - move cursor by word
  ctrl+g - edit prompt in external editor

Agent environment
  /init - Initialize Copilot instructions for this repository, or suppress the init suggestion

Models and subagents

Code
  /ide - Connect to an IDE workspace

Permissions
  /allow-all - Enable all permissions (tools, paths, and URLs)

Session
  /resume - Switch to a different session (optionally specify session ID or task ID)
